Your rig is telling you something when torque starts climbing mid-bore.
As the drill string gets longer, more pipe is in contact with the bore wall. More contact means more friction. More friction means higher torque readings, harder pullback, and faster wear on your tooling.

That's the problem Torque Down solves.

It's an oil-based liquid lubricant you add straight to your fluid. It coats the pipe and the bore wall with a protective film that cuts friction across the full length of the string.

Standard dose is 2 L/m³. Add it at mix-up. If torque starts climbing mid-job, top up with another dose. It's compatible with bentonite and polymer systems, so it fits into whatever program you're already running.

Less drag on the string. Lower pullback forces. Longer life on your bits and steering gear.

Friday we'll go deeper on when you need Torque Down and when you can get away without it.
When do you usually notice torque becoming a problem on your jobs?

A bore without lubrication is a bore that's fighting you every metre.
Torque Down works across more drilling disciplines than most people realise. HDD, waterwell, diamond coring. Sand and gravel, heavy rock, reactive clay. If there's pipe in the ground and friction on the string, it has a job to do.

It pairs with whatever fluid system you're running. Bentonite-based, polymer-based, doesn't matter. Add 2 L/m³ at mix-up and it goes to work.

Where it really earns its keep: long HDD shots where friction compounds over distance. Large diameter bores where more surface area means more drag. Deep waterwells where you're running hundreds of metres of string.

For standard bores in easy ground, you might not need it. For anything where bore length, diameter, or ground conditions are working against you, it pays for itself in reduced wear and smoother pullback.

For tougher conditions, give one of our team a call. We'll dial in the right program for the ground.
If you've never tried Torque Down, talk to us about your next job. We'll help you work out if it's worth adding to your program.
